turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Parking was a shocker, sorry. He's been a bit clingy out in the waiting room too.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): All good. What's brought him in?
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Leo's two. Fever and a cough. Started Tuesday, so that's three days.
[SEG0004] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah nah, longer than that. He was warm on the weekend already. I'd say five days, maybe six.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): So somewhere between three and six days. Leo, does your tummy hurt?
[SEG0006] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you been coughing?
[SEG0008] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has though. Dry barking cough, kept us up half the night. He'll just say no to you.
[SEG0010] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the cough's been the whole time, not just since Tuesday.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any hard breathing? Pulling in under the ribs?
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Breathing looks normal to me.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Runny nose?
[SEG0014] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Snotty since the weekend, yeah.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting?
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomits. He grabbed his right ear yesterday and said it was sore.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Leo, is your ear sore?
[SEG0018] person_4 (PATIENT): Ear.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Eating and drinking?
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Drinking alright. Not eating much, and he's a bit flat.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weeing as usual?
[SEG0022] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah. Pull-ups overnight, still wet in the morning. Not dry.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, random one, but did you catch the footy? Madness.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any rash?
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No rash.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): How high has the temperature gone at home?
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thirty eight point seven on our thermometer this morning.
[SEG0028] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That one's dodgy. I got thirty nine point four last night. Checked it twice.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): What have you given him?
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Panadol. The one that's a hundred and twenty milligrams in five mils. One spoon, roughly every four hours.
[SEG0031] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two spoons this morning, not one. And last night I gave him Nurofen, one spoon of that.
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We didn't even open the Nurofen. Last night was Panadol too. One spoon. Well, I wasn't up this morning, so maybe you did do two then.
[SEG0033] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I definitely did two spoons of the Panadol this morning. Alright, maybe last night wasn't Nurofen.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, paracetamol, and the dose is a bit all over the shop. Any allergies?
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. None.
[SEG0036] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hang on. My mum reckons he came up in a rash with penicillin when he was a baby. Nothing written down, mind you.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I've never heard that. He had amoxicillin last winter and he was completely fine.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll leave that as not clear. Anyone else crook at home?
[SEG0039] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His sister had a cold last week. He's at daycare most days.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Asthma? Any lung trouble? Any operations?
[SEG0041] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No asthma, no lung problems, no operations. No regular medicines either.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anyone smoking at home?
[SEG0043] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I quit, um, two years back. She never has.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll have a look. Temp is thirty seven point nine, heart rate a hundred and twenty, breathing rate twenty eight, sats ninety eight on air.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear, no wheeze. Throat's a bit red. Right eardrum looks dull.
[SEG0046] person_4 (PATIENT): Ow.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry mate. Tummy's soft. No neck stiffness.

[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Most likely a viral upper airway infection. That night cough could be a bit of croup, and there may be an early ear infection. I can't rule out a bacterial otitis, but I wouldn't start antibiotics today.
[SEG0049] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So we just watch him?
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Push the fluids. For his age stick to one five mil spoon of that hundred and twenty in five paracetamol, every four to six hours, not two spoons. Leave the ibuprofen.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the fever or the cough hasn't settled in a few days, we might do a chest x-ray. Not booking one now.
[SEG0052] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): When do we come back?

[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's see him in two weeks. Sooner if he's working to breathe, the fever goes back over thirty nine, or he stops drinking. If the ear is still sore in forty eight hours we might start amoxicillin, but only after we sort the penicillin thing. Reception will book the two weeks on your way out.

omissions.text: Home temperature measurements were 38.7 C this morning and 39.4 C last night (checked twice), indicating fever over 39 at home.
Paracetamol formulation strength used at home was 120 mg/5 mL.
Reported home paracetamol doses were inconsistent: roughly 5 mL every 4 hours initially, definitely 10 mL this morning, and 5 mL last night.
Ibuprofen/Nurofen use was disputed: one family member said one spoon was given last night, then this was retracted and they said the Nurofen was not opened.

Allergy history was not simply negative: possible rash with penicillin in infancy was reported by one family member, but another said he tolerated amoxicillin last winter, and the doctor concluded the penicillin allergy status was unclear.
Sibling had a cold last week.
Doctor stated they would not start antibiotics today.
